title: Etale locally closed exceptional restriction and finite quotient coefficients
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\ge m\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$ with the quotient map. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion, $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open, and $s=gj$. Work exclusively on small etale sites, with constant coefficient rings and ordinary unbounded module derived categories. Set $Rs_{!,A}=g_{*,A}j_!$, $Rs_A^!=j^*Rg_A^!$, where $g_*\dashv Rg^!$ is the ordinary etale closed exceptional adjunction, and similarly over $B$. Let $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ on each scheme $T$; let $D^b_{ctf}$ mean bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, tested against all degree-zero module sheaves.

For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, put $N_g=Rg_A^!M$. Both $N_g$ and $j^*N_g$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible. Let $c_{g,N} : F_Xg_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{*,B}F_ZN$ be the canonical direct-image coefficient comparison, adjoint to coefficient change of the ordinary inverse-image/direct-image counit. The map
$$b_{g,M}:F_ZN_g\longrightarrow Rg_B^!F_XM$$
adjoint under $g_{*,B}\dashv Rg_B^!$ to $F_X(\epsilon_{g,A,M})\circ c_{g,N_g}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Put $b_{s,M}=j^*b_{g,M}$ after restriction/scalar identification. For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let
$$q_{s,P}=g_{*,B}(q_{j,P})\circ c_{g,j_!P}:F_XRs_{!,A}P\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_{!,B}F_SP,$$
where $q_j$ is the open extension/scalar isomorphism restricting to the identity. Then $b_{s,M}$ and $q_{s,P}$ are natural isomorphisms, $Rs_{!,A}\dashv Rs_A^!$ has counit $\epsilon_{s,A}=\epsilon_{g,A}\circ g_{*,A}(\epsilon_{j,A})$, and
$$\epsilon_{s,B,F_XM}\circ Rs_{!,B}(b_{s,M})\circ q_{s,Rs_A^!M}=F_X(\epsilon_{s,A,M}).$$
For $S=Z$ this specializes to the closed case. No pro-etale exceptional adjoint is used.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], [def-kun-tor-amplitude], [lem-exc-closed-ambient], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor].

proof.text: Write $u:V=X\setminus g(Z)\hookrightarrow X$ for the complementary open, reserving $j$ for $S\hookrightarrow Z$. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, the intersection with $Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, so $Z$ is finite type over $k$. Both $X$ and $Z$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and their open subschemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. All these open immersions are quasi-compact: their inverse images in affine opens are opens in Noetherian spaces. Hence $u$ and $j$ are finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]; they are separated since their diagonals are identities. Thus $V,S,Z$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The rings $A,B$ are finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Moreover $B$ is a finite $A$-module, being a quotient of $A$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: hypotheses for the closed-support route; Stacks 01T6 and the affine quotient description

proof.text: Choose a nonnegative finite cohomological-dimension bound $c$ for $Ru_*$ using [lem-etale-finite-type-sep-closed-derived-dimension], increasing its integer bound to its maximum with zero. Its hypotheses hold because $k$ is algebraically closed and the additive group of $A$ is torsion. Every constructible $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $V$ has bounded constructible $Ru_*H$ by [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type]. The prime-to-characteristic hypothesis holds: by clause (5) of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], in the DVR $\mathcal O_E$ write $\ell=v\varpi_E^e$ with $v$ a unit and $e\ge1$; for $er\ge n$ the integer $\ell^r$ annihilates $A$ and is invertible in $k$. In particular all $R^qu_*H$ are constructible. Choose a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $M$. Apply [prop-exc-closed-tor] to $g,u,A,M,c$. It proves that $N=Rg_A^!M$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[a,b+c+1]$. This is the ambient ordinary étale adjoint in that node, with no pro-étale replacement.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, finite-Tor closed exceptional restriction; Stacks 0F10 and the cited closed-support Tor theorem

proof.text: We need the étale restrictions $u^*M$ and $j^*N$ to be in $D^b_{ctf}$. Inverse image on constant-ring module sheaves is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. It commutes with cohomology, and constructibility of the underlying sheaves is preserved by [prop-constructible-pullback]. For the Tor condition take a bounded flat model using the explicit small-étale clause of [lem-sf-flat-model]. This model is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat]. The ringed-topos pullback of this model has flat terms and is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; inverse image is this module pullback because the coefficient ring is constant. It remains in the same finite range. Tensoring this flat model with any degree-zero module sheaf computes derived tensor and has terms only in that range. This gives the required Tor bound, for $u^*M$ and for $j^*N$. The same pullback/tensor comparison, or the open-restriction comparison of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], supplies the natural scalar identification $F_Vu^*\cong u^*F_X$ and $F_Sj^*\cong j^*F_Z$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, restriction to the stratum; small-étale flat-model argument and Stacks 07A4/0G7E

proof.text: For either coefficient ring, $g_*$ is exact and fully faithful on the ordinary derived categories. Here is the passage from sheaves to complexes used below. The closed-support equivalence [lem-kun-04ca] is fully faithful and has left inverse $g^*$ on abelian sheaves. It lifts to constant-ring module sheaves by transporting each scalar endomorphism; faithfulness transports the ring-action equations and detects linearity of morphisms. The natural stalk formula [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] gives the original stalk on $Z$; off $Z$ the stalk is zero by the essential-image clause of [lem-kun-04ca]. Exactness of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and their conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] therefore show $g_*$ is exact on module sheaves. The exact $g^*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and $g_*$ descend termwise, together with their adjunction and invertible counit $g^*g_*\cong1$. Indeed the termwise unit, counit and triangle identities descend along localization. This proves derived full faithfulness. In particular $g_*$ reflects isomorphisms, and for $L$ in its image the map $\operatorname{Hom}(L,g_*Rg^!T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(L,T)$ induced by the exceptional counit is bijective: write $L=g_*Q$ and use full faithfulness and $g_*\dashv Rg^!$ from [lem-exc-closed-ambient].

source.place: Stacks 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward), 04FX and 03PU; module and derived passage written out

proof.text: By [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], applied only to its ordinary étale clause, there are natural isomorphisms $c_{u,u^*M}:F_XRu_{*,A}u^*M\cong Ru_{*,B}F_Vu^*M$ and $c_{g,N}:F_Xg_{*,A}N\cong g_{*,B}F_ZN$. All their inputs are bounded constructible finite-Tor by Steps 2–3, and the geometric and coefficient hypotheses were checked in Step 1. Put $d=Ru_{*,B}(F_Vu^*M\cong u^*F_XM)\circ c_{u,u^*M}$. This is the isomorphism on the third terms of the two closed-support triangles. The definition of $c$ here is exactly the inverse-image/direct-image counit transpose required in the statement, not an arbitrary projection-formula isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: move finite coefficient change through the complementary open direct image

proof.text: Let $\eta_A:M\to Ru_{*,A}u^*M$ and $\eta_B:F_XM\to Ru_{*,B}u^*F_XM$ be the ordinary units. Then $d\circ F_X\eta_A=\eta_B$. To check this equality, transpose both maps by $u^*\dashv Ru_{*,B}$. By the defining counit normalization of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], the transpose of the left side, under the open scalar identifications of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], is $F_V(\varepsilon^A_{u,u^*M}\circ u^*\eta_A)=F_V(1_{u^*M})$. This is the identity by the adjunction triangle identity. The transpose of $\eta_B$ is also the identity. The Hom bijection therefore gives the displayed equality. This calculation is in $B$-module derived categories even when $B$ is not flat over $A$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, normalization of the open-unit square; adjunction transpose expanded

proof.text: Use [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] over $A$ at $M$ and over $B$ at $F_XM$. Apply the exact triangulated scalar functor [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the first triangle, obtaining $F_Xg_*N\to F_XM\to F_XRu_*u^*M\to$. The second triangle is $g_{*,B}Rg_B^!F_XM\to F_XM\to Ru_{*,B}u^*F_XM\to$. Step 6 gives a square on the middle and third terms with maps $1$ and $d$. Rotate both distinguished triangles and apply TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], then rotate back. It supplies a first map $t:F_Xg_*N\to g_{*,B}Rg_B^!F_XM$ and a morphism of triangles $(t,1,d)$. Since $1$ and $d$ are isomorphisms, [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] implies that $t$ is an isomorphism. Its first square says $\varepsilon_{g,B,F_XM}\circ t=F_X\varepsilon_{g,A,M}$.

By the adjoint definition of $b=b_{g,M}$ in the statement, $\varepsilon_{g,B,F_XM}\circ g_{*,B}b\circ c_{g,N}=F_X\varepsilon_{g,A,M}$. Thus $t$ and $g_{*,B}b\circ c_{g,N}$ have the same composite with the exceptional counit. Their source is $F_Xg_*N\cong g_{*,B}F_ZN$, in the image of the fully faithful closed direct image. The bijection proved in Step 4 makes the two maps equal. Since $t$ and $c_{g,N}$ are isomorphisms, so is $g_{*,B}b$, and reflection from Step 4 proves that $b$ is an isomorphism. No uniqueness of arbitrary cone completions was assumed. Naturality of $b$ follows by transposing the natural transformation $F_X\varepsilon_{g,A}\circ c_g^{-1}$ through the natural Hom bijection of [lem-exc-closed-ambient], using naturality of $c_g$ from [lem-coef-finite-direct-image].

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: identify the support-triangle comparison with the specified exceptional transpose

proof.text: For $P\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the complex $j_!P$ is bounded constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]: its cohomology is $j_!\mathcal H^r(P)$. For a degree-zero module sheaf $H$ on $Z$, [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor] identifies $j_!P\otimes_A^LH$ with $j_!(P\otimes_A^Lj^*H)$. Exactness of restriction and of $j_!$ gives the same finite Tor bound as for $P$. Hence [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] applies to $g$ at $j_!P$. Its $c_{g,j_!P}$ followed by $g_{*,B}q_{j,P}$ is the natural isomorphism $q_{s,P}$ of the statement. Also $b_{s,M}$ is the restriction of the isomorphism of Step 8 after the scalar/restriction identification of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], so it is a natural isomorphism. Step 3 already proved that its $A$-source before coefficient change is bounded constructible finite-Tor.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, extension by zero and compact-support coefficient identification; Stacks 03DJ and constructible extension by zero

proof.text: The closed adjunction of [lem-exc-closed-ambient] and the derived open adjunction, with its degreewise counit normalization in [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], compose. Explicitly the two Hom bijections are $\operatorname{Hom}_X(g_*j_!P,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(j_!P,Rg^!M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(P,j^*Rg^!M)$. They are natural in both variables, hence give $Rs_!\dashv Rs^!$. The inverse bijections send the identity of $j^*Rg^!M$ first to $\varepsilon_{j,Rg^!M}$ and then to $\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ g_*\varepsilon_{j,Rg^!M}$. This is the asserted composite counit over either $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: composition of the closed and open adjunctions and its counit

proof.text:
Set $N=Rg_A^!M$, $N'=Rg_B^!F_XM$ and write $b:F_ZN\to N'$. Suppress only the canonical open scalar identifications, so $b_s=j^*b$. Expand the left side of the desired identity using Step 10 and the definition of $q_s$; it is
$$\varepsilon_{g,B}\,g_{*,B}(\varepsilon_{j,B,N'})\,g_{*,B}j_!(j^*b)\,g_{*,B}q_{j,j^*N}\,c_{g,j_!j^*N}.$$
Naturality of the open counit changes its two middle factors to $g_{*,B}b\,g_{*,B}\varepsilon_{j,B,F_ZN}$. The open coefficient-counit identity of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor] then changes $\varepsilon_{j,B,F_ZN}q_{j,j^*N}$ to $F_Z\varepsilon_{j,A,N}$. Naturality of $c_g$ in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], at the morphism $\varepsilon_{j,A,N}:j_!j^*N\to N$, gives
$$g_{*,B}(F_Z\varepsilon_{j,A,N})\,c_{g,j_!j^*N}=c_{g,N}\,F_X(g_{*,A}\varepsilon_{j,A,N}).$$
The closed transpose identity of Step 8 now makes the whole expression
$$F_X\varepsilon_{g,A,M}\,F_X(g_{*,A}\varepsilon_{j,A,N})=F_X\varepsilon_{s,A,M}.$$
All coefficient comparisons used here are defined on their stated domains: $N,j^*N,j_!j^*N$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible by Steps 2, 3 and 9. This proves the specified equality, including its actual morphisms.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4: exceptional-counit compatibility, expanded as a composition calculation

proof.text: If $S=Z$ and $j=1_Z$, restriction and extension by zero are identities. The normalized open scalar comparison restricts to the identity everywhere, hence $q_j=1$ by [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Thus $Rs_!=g_*$, $Rs^!=Rg^!$, $q_s=c_g$, and $b_s=b_g$; the last equality becomes precisely the closed transpose identity of Step 8. This proves the closed specialization as well.

lean.note: Ordinary unbounded small-etale constant-module categories only. Canonical closed coefficient map is the exceptional adjunction transpose of the inverse of the recorded direct-image comparison followed by scalar extension of its counit. The inverse is extended by zero outside its isomorphism locus; the theorem explicitly asserts its invertibility on every input used. The full comparison predicate spells out the two finite-Tor constructibility assertions, the isomorphism assertions, naturality and the pasted counit equation. The added landed dependencies supply the existing quotient map between arbitrary coefficient stages and the already published ordinary-etale finite-Tor constructible predicate. No second D^b_ctf definition is made.
